data.body_html:
An Estepona boat rental with snorkeling gear provided is the smartest way to explore the Costa del Sol’s clearest waters without packing a thing. Every charter from our Puerto Banús fleet includes masks, fins, and snorkels, plus a licensed skipper who knows exactly where the fish hide. Whether you’re after a quick 2-hour escape or a full day on the water, you’ll anchor at secret coves like Cala del Faro and Cala Cortés — spots most tourists never see.

Why Choose Estepona for Snorkeling?

Estepona’s coastline is quieter than Marbella’s, with rocky reefs and sandy patches that attract bream, wrasse, and occasional octopus. The water clarity often exceeds 10 metres on calm days. Unlike the crowded beaches of the Golden Mile, Estepona’s coves are sheltered and shallow, making them ideal for families and beginners. The best part? You don’t need to drive or queue — your private boat takes you straight there.

Our Fleet for Snorkeling Charters

We have boats for every group size and budget. All depart from Puerto Banús, just 15 minutes east of Estepona. Here’s a quick comparison:

Prices for the Astondoa 40 and Azimut 39 start at €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for 8 hours — all inclusive. For the Mangusta 80 (white or grey), the minimum charter is 4 hours at €4,719, which includes a free jet ski. All other boats are priced on request via WhatsApp.

Best Hidden Coves Near Estepona

Our skippers know the coastline intimately. These are the top spots for snorkeling:

  • Cala del Faro — Rocky bottom, 2–6m depth, excellent for experienced snorkelers. Located just east of Estepona port.
  • Cala Cortés — Sandy entry, calm waters, perfect for children. About 10 minutes west of Puerto Banús.
  • Playa del Saladillo — Shallow and sheltered, with seagrass beds that attract small fish.
  • Río Verde — A river mouth with mixed sand and rock; good for spotting rays.

All are within a 20-minute cruise from Puerto Banús. Your skipper will choose the best spot based on wind and tide conditions.

What Snorkeling Gear Is Provided?

We supply full snorkel sets: silicone masks, adjustable fins, and dry-top snorkels. Life jackets are available for non-swimmers. There’s no extra charge — just hop off the boat and dive in. If you need prescription masks or wetsuits, bring your own; the water in summer (June–September) is typically 20–26°C, so wetsuits are optional.

Sample Itinerary: 4-Hour Snorkeling Trip

Here’s what a typical half-day looks like:

  • 10:00 — Depart Puerto Banús. Enjoy coffee and pastries on board.
  • 10:20 — Arrive at Cala del Faro. Snorkel for 45 minutes.
  • 11:15 — Cruise west along the coast, spotting La Concha mountain.
  • 11:30 — Anchor at Cala Cortés for a second snorkel session.
  • 12:15 — Light snacks, beer, and cava while floating.
  • 12:45 — Return to Puerto Banús.

Longer charters (6–8 hours) can include a stop at a beach club or lunch at a chiringuito.
